title: Secrets and key rotation
explain: Store secrets in managed stores; rotate; never commit credentials; least privilege service users. (Tier 1–2 simulation fidelity — verify production details in official SAP docs.)
analogy: Think of "Secrets and key rotation" as a named building block you must explain under pressure.
whyItMatters: Without Secrets and key rotation, you mis-diagnose incidents and make weak architecture choices.

howToApply: Use Secrets and key rotation explicitly in a design defense sentence
mnemonic: NAME IT TO TAME IT: Say “Secrets and key rotation” + one failure mode out loud — if you can't, you don't own it yet. (Secrets → mechanism → failure)
useCases: Greenfield design workshop: decide if “Secrets and key rotation” is required given constraints (latency, clean-core, team skills).
Incident bridge: symptoms appear; use “Secrets and key rotation” to classify the failing hop before changing config.
Architecture review board: defend why you accepted residual risk around “Secrets and key rotation”.
